chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibn al-Husayn, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The hypocritical woman is not married off to the believing woman, and the believing woman is married off to the hypocritical woman.

key_terms.الْمُنَافِقَةُ: The hypocritical woman (female counterpart of the hypocrite)
key_terms.تُتَزَوَّجُ: Is married off (passive voice, indicating the act of arranging marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a hypocritical woman to a believing woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *kafa'ah* (compatibility) by prioritizing religious piety (*iman*) over other social factors, ensuring that a believer is not spiritually compromised by a hypocrite. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on inner faith as the primary criterion for marital harmony and spiritual integrity within the family unit. The prohibition serves to protect the religious environment of the household from the subtle influences of hypocrisy, which can erode sincere devotion.
